newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union says banks face strike over sick pay.
newsitem.headline: German union says banks face strike over sick pay.

text.p: Germany's banks face warning strikes like those already staged in the engineering sector if they stick to their guns on implementing a cut in sick pay, the HBV retail, bank and insurance union said on Wednesday.

"Reactions so far among bank employees have been more than hefty. We therefore expect there will be protests in the banking sector as well if employers reject a solution," HBV board member Klaus Carlin said in a radio interview.
"I am not ruling out warning strikes."
A working group of union and bank representatives met on Wednesday in Frankfurt for talks and an HBV spokeswoman said sick pay would be on the agenda.
A spokesman for Commerzbank AG, which hosted the meeting, said the talks had been scheduled for some time and were routine discussions concerning conditions of employment in the banking sector.

The German Association of Bank Employers said last week banks would implement a cut in pay to 80 percent of full pay during sickness, in line with new government legislation enabling employers to do so.

More than 120,000 engineering workers across Germany downed tools and took to the streets on Tuesday in protest at the decision by major industrial companies like Daimler-Benz AG to cut sick pay. The law took effect on Tuesday.
A spokesman for Commerzbank AG said his bank had implemented the sick pay cut on October 1.
